question: In AEMO's dispatch data, how do InitialSupply and ClearedSupply differ, in particular in terms of which point of the interval each one refers to?

answer_as_displayed.headline: “Cleared Supply is forecast scheduled demand to be met at the end of the interval.” [c1]
summary: “Initial Supply is actual scheduled demand measured or estimated at the beginning of an interval.” [c1]
“Cleared Supply is forecast scheduled demand to be met at the end of the interval.” [c1]

Initial Supply is the sum, at the start of each interval, of generation from all scheduled and semi-scheduled generating units within the region plus the net interconnector flow into the region (as measured at the inter-regional boundary). [c1]
Cleared Supply is the sum of the dispatch targets for all scheduled and semi-scheduled generating units within the region plus the net target interconnector flow into the region. [c1]

“InitialSupply = Sum of generation InitialMW over all regional scheduled and semi-scheduled generating units + scheduled BDUs + net MeteredMWFlow into the region over all interconnectors connected to the region” [c2]

“ClearedSupply = Sum of generation TotalCleared over all regional scheduled and semi-scheduled generating units + scheduled BDUs + net MWFlow into the region over all interconnectors connected to the region” [c2]
“In Dispatch, InitialMW and MeteredMWFlow are actual metered values (i.e. SCADA values).” [c2]

“In Pre-dispatch and 5MPD, InitialMW and MeteredMWFlow are actual metered values only in the first interval and in subsequent intervals these values are based on the targets of the previous interval.” [c2]
